text:
Temporal attention offers a practical extension within BERT4Rec. [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) established joint modeling of absolute positions and pairwise elapsed-time relations; its temporal mechanism is relevant without adopting its causal backbone. More recently, [FuXi-γ (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12740) introduced tunable exponential-power encoding of relative time intervals to capture short- and long-term preferences. Its decoder-only architecture should not replace BERT4Rec; the transferable idea is a jointly learned temporal decay function.

[TSAPE (WWW 2026)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3774904.3792333) models sequences of inter-event intervals using convolution and attention, then integrates the resulting adaptive features with positional encoding. This suggests learning context-dependent temporal relevance rather than uniformly suppressing older events. Its interpretation of interaction gaps as dwell-time feedback needs caution for Amazon purchase histories: elapsed purchase time does not directly measure engagement. These papers provide design precedents, not evidence of gains under the pinned RecHarness evaluation.

A suitable experimental hypothesis is per-head attention logits augmented by a learned log-bucketed elapsed-time bias, optionally with a nonnegative learned decay penalty. This is a proposed adaptation, not a verified result from those papers. Keep all components jointly trained inside one bidirectional BERT4Rec network per category. Train on strict prefixes ending in MASK, using only timestamps available within each prefix; anchor MASK temporal features to the last observed event or use a learned unknown-time representation, never the held-out target timestamp. Apply identical construction during appended-MASK inference and read the final nonpadding MASK position. Compare against the corrected baseline using macro validation HR@10.
